title: Materials table
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y6 lesson 3 (Materials table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 3: Shadows: shape and position. To understand how shadows form and why their shape and position change

questions.q: Why does a shadow have the same shape as the object?
questions.a: Light travels in straight lines and is blocked by the object's outline
questions.model: Light goes straight past the edges, but not through the object. So the dark area has the object's outline.

questions.q: Read the chart: when was the shadow shortest?
Is frosted glass opaque, translucent or transparent?
With a torch, test six materials at home and sort them into transparent, translucent and opaque. Record in the table.
questions.a: Pupils' own; for example foil opaque, tissue translucent, cling film transparent
questions.model: Teacher tests a plastic bag on camera: 'Some light through, fuzzy shadow: translucent.'

questions.q: Explain the chart's pattern using the height of the Sun.
questions.a: The Sun is highest around midday so shadows are shortest; low Sun in morning and evening gives long shadows.

questions.q: Why is the shadow on the other side in the evening?
questions.a: The Sun has moved across the sky from east to west.

questions.q: A shadow forms when light is...
Big question: why is your shadow long in the morning?
questions.a: The Sun is low, so the light hits at a low angle and makes a long shadow.
